card werk-contract-waiver-reason  [decided]
A waiver of a contract fact needs a written reason
why: A waiver leaves a required fact empty on purpose. Without a written reason, a reader later cannot tell a deliberate waiver from a forgotten fact.
subtree: 1 card, 1 decided

The decide check lets a card go without a basis, or without a weighed option, when the author waives that fact (#werk-contract-facts). Every escape hatch of a check leaves a written reason (#pr-gate), so a waiver does too.

- The basis waiver says why no decided card is a basis, for example that the card is the root of a tree.
- The option waiver says why no option was weighed against the card (#werk-contract-guess).
- A waiver with an empty reason is refused.
- The reason is stored with the waiver and prints wherever the card prints.
- Who decides is not waivable. A kill criterion that names no metric already carries its reason.

```
 T  no basis, who: me

 decide                              refused   no basis
 waive the basis, no reason          refused   a waiver needs a reason
 waive the basis: "root of a tree"   allowed
 decide                              passes    T prints "basis waived: root of a tree"

 U  who: you, no option weighed

 decide                              refused   no option
 waive the option, no reason         refused   a waiver needs a reason
 waive the option: "no real choice"  allowed
 decide                              passes    U prints "option waived: no real choice"
```

  -> refines         werk-contract  A card cannot become decided until a program check passes
  -> depends_on      pr-gate  A written rule is enforced by a check when a record moves to a new state
       why: takes the rule that every escape hatch leaves a written reason
       STALE — from a reopen further upstream, open #pr-gate to trace it
  -> depends_on      werk-contract-facts  A card needs four facts before it is decided
       why: takes the basis fact and the option fact that a waiver can leave empty
       STALE — from a reopen further upstream, open #werk-contract-facts to trace it
  -> depends_on      werk-contract-guess  Unchallenged is a recorded fact, not a value derived from the data
       why: takes the option waiver, which is a stated fact stored on the log
       STALE — from a reopen further upstream, open #werk-contract-guess to trace it
  <- alternative_to  werk-contract-waiver-reason:opt0  A waiver is a bare flag with no reason
  <- alternative_to  werk-contract-waiver-reason:opt1  Only the basis waiver needs a reason
  <- depends_on      werk-contract-amend-who  Who decides and a waiver on a decided card change only by an amend
Options
  werk-contract-waiver-reason:opt0  A waiver is a bare flag with no reason
    why not: A waiver would then leave nothing to read, and a deliberate waiver looks the same as a forgotten fact.
  werk-contract-waiver-reason:opt1  Only the basis waiver needs a reason
    why not: The option waiver hides the same kind of gap. A card with no option and no reason cannot be told from a card whose option was lost.

card werk-propose-new  [decided]
A new card is a proposal too, not a direct append
why: Cards nobody decided are fuzzy, unbelievable, and indistinguishable from decided ones once they are in the log.
subtree: 8 cards, 5 open, 3 decided, 2 stale

Creation follows the same staged path as an edit (#al-diff-cli). Adding a card keeps its name, has no bypass, and always stages. Its output says "proposed", not "added".

Every kind stages, not only `card`. A `source`, an `option`, and an `excerpt` each wait for the same ✓. An option node carries a why-not reason the agent wrote; that reason is exactly the kind of invented content the accept gate exists to catch.
